- Overestimate prices in the short term after strong positive sentiment spikes; model tends to lag or overreact to sentiment peaks.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is weak or negative; model often fails to capture downward momentum or mean reversion.
- Overshoot upward after recent price spikes; model tends to overcorrect or overestimate continuation of rally.
- Underestimate upward momentum when sentiment is mildly positive but recent prices are falling; model misses early reversal signals.
- Overestimate downward moves when sentiment is mildly negative; model underweights sentiment-driven downside risk.
- Model tends to underestimate true price volatility in the 30-day horizon, especially when sentiment is volatile or mixed.
- When sentiment is consistently positive over 3–5 days, model should adjust upward bias by 5–10% to reflect sentiment momentum.
- When sentiment is negative and prices are trending down, model should avoid sharp downward corrections; instead, apply gradual mean reversion.
- Model often underestimates price peaks in the final 5–7 days of forecast horizon; adjust upward by 2–5% for final days if sentiment is positive.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed, model should avoid extreme forecasts; use 1–2% buffer around historical mean to avoid overfitting.
